about:
Mitsubishi International Food Ingredients, Inc. (MIFI) operates its Dublin, Ohio office as part of a wholly-owned subsidiary of Mitsubishi Corporation. The company has refined its network of food-grade warehouses and carrier partnerships since 2004, building a distribution infrastructure that spans the United States.

MIFI sources and distributes more than 1,000 food, nutritional, and pharmaceutical ingredients, including custom seasoning blends developed through its formulation and applications expertise. All warehouses are GMP-compliant and FDA-registered, and the company manages a fleet of LTL and TL carriers that adhere to federal and state requirements. Over 90 percent of customers receive next-day service from its prepared and well-stocked facilities.

The company serves consumer packaged goods (CPG) companies ranging from large corporations to small independent shops across industries such as food, nutrition and supplements, pharmaceuticals, biotech, cosmetics, and pet products. Its quality assurance team, staffed by professionals certified in PCQI, FSVP, HACCP, and cGMP, engages directly with global supply chain partners to verify supplier qualifications.

MIFI differentiates itself through a dedicated customer service model that avoids third-party call centers, guaranteeing direct access to empowered representatives. The team proactively monitors order fulfillment, confirms forecasts, and explores flexible shipping options to meet go-to-market deadlines, reflecting a mission to deliver beyond expectations while operating to the highest ethical and safety standards.

Mize & Co., Inc., operating as Mize Wire Products, has been based in Kingman, Kansas since its founding in 1936. The company began as a manufacturer and wholesale distributor of electrical components, though the names of its founders are not publicly documented. Over eight decades, it has remained a fixture in the region’s industrial supply chain.

The firm produces custom wire harnesses and cable assemblies, and stocks a broad range of electrical parts including connectors, terminals, fuses, wire, clamps, nylon ties, and pre‑assembled kits. Its in‑house process covers quoting, drawing, manufacturing, and delivery, allowing it to turn around custom orders quickly. No facility size or headcount figures are disclosed.

Mize serves the automotive, agricultural, and industrial sectors, selling to distributors, retailers, and original equipment manufacturers. Its harnesses and cables are built to the specifications of customers in those industries, while its catalog of electrical pieces supports maintenance and assembly operations across the same markets.

The company emphasizes its long‑term commitment to quality and its ability to quote, draw, manufacture, and deliver rapidly. That end‑to‑end capability, combined with an 80‑plus‑year track record, is presented as its core differentiator.

name: Modern Alpha Plastics Inc
old_description: Modern Alpha Plastics was formed in 1996 when two of Kansas City's most respected custom molders — Modern Plastics Molding (founded 1965) and Alpha Plastics — merged into a single shop with sixty combined years of precision injection experience.
about:
The company was formed in 1996 when Modern Plastics Molding (founded 1965 in Independence, Missouri) and Alpha Plastics (a Kansas City molder founded in the early 1960s) merged, combining sixty years of precision injection molding experience. Today the business is led by Anthony C. Gross, President and Chief Engineer, who oversees quoting and mold approvals directly.

The shop runs twenty-one injection molding presses ranging from 50 to 1,550 tons of clamp force, with shot capacities of 2 to 75 ounces and part weights from 5 grams to 10 pounds. Production volumes span 250 to over five million parts annually. In-house capabilities cover mold design, build, qualification, repair, and maintenance through vetted tooling partners, plus secondary operations including ultrasonic welding, CNC machining, sub-assembly, custom packaging, heat sealing, and pad printing. The company processes nine engineering-grade resin families along with commodity, glass-filled, mineral-filled, and impact-modified materials.

Modern Alpha serves aerospace and defense (ITAR-registered), medical device, drone and UAS, consumer, and industrial markets. Specific programs include structural drone brackets, legacy OEM re-engineering, metals-to-plastics conversions, thin-wall food-grade containers, and large industrial housings. Customers range from OEMs requiring close-tolerance components to firms needing turnkey design-to-distribution support.

The company emphasizes engineer-led, single-source responsibility — design, tooling, molding, assembly, and shipping under one purchase order. Statistical Process Control and Statistical Quality Control run on every press every shift, with material inspection at receiving, in-process evaluation, pre-shipping sign-off, and retained samples archived indefinitely. Long-tenured operators, some with thirty-year careers, provide tribal knowledge that the firm cites as a deliberate competitive advantage.

name: Modern Metal Company
old_description: Custom metal fabrication solutions for residential and commercial projects since 2020.
about:
Modern Metal Company operates from Lowell, Arkansas, where it was founded in 2020 by Victor Onishenko. The business began as a custom metal fabrication shop serving residential and commercial projects across Northwest Arkansas and Southwest Missouri.

The company fabricates custom metal railings, including staircase, spiral staircase, and floating staircase systems, along with its proprietary Levaplate® leveling system that uses set screws to eliminate washers and shims. In-house capabilities cover welding in stainless steel, aluminum, and steel, premium powder coating on all products, and full installation services. To date, the shop has installed more than 150 custom railings.

Customers include builders and homeowners constructing or remodeling higher-end homes in Northwest Arkansas and the Joplin, Missouri area, as well as elderly clients needing handrails. The company also takes on commercial projects requiring architectural metalwork.

Modern Metal Company emphasizes a 6-to-8-week lead time, well below the industry norm of 8 to 12 months, and provides direct communication with the owner, free shop drawings, and a turnkey service from quote through installation and cleanup. The Levaplate® system and hidden-hardware design are cited as key differentiators.

name: Modern Process Equipment Corporation
old_description: OPTIMIZE YOUR PROCESS WITH THE WORLD'S LEADING MANUFACTURER OF
about:
Modern Process Equipment Corporation was founded in 1957 in Chicago, Illinois, where it maintains its worldwide headquarters. The company remains a family-owned business that has spent more than six decades designing, manufacturing, and supporting industrial process equipment for customers around the globe.

MPE builds precision particle-size-reduction equipment — including corrugated roller mills sold under the Gran-U-Lizer™ name, disc-style and roller-style coffee grinders (such as the compact SRM.MAX for espresso), and the Chain-Vey® tubular drag conveyor line for gentle, enclosed transport of bulk powders and fragile food products. The Process Systems Group integrates those machines into turnkey lines that handle classification, storage, pneumatic transport, mixing, coffee degassing, and clean-in-place automation. The company also operates grind and conveyor testing labs and runs an exchange program that restores worn rolls and heads to original condition.

The equipment serves coffee roasters (gourmet, industrial, capsule, turkish, and ultrafine), food processors (bakery, cereal, snack, peanut and tree nut, pet food), chemical and mineral producers, distilleries, breweries, and powder-and-bulk-solids handlers. Named references include Death Wish Coffee Company, Lawrence Foods, Westrock, Wicked Joe Coffee, Bird Foods, Pacifikava, a aviation supplier, a CPG brand, and a snack brand.

MPE states its purpose is to lead the invention, development, and manufacture of the industry's most advanced processing equipment and to translate that technology into customer value through professional solutions and unwavering support — including 24/7/365 virtual assistance, global on-site service on short notice, commissioning support, and operator training.

name: Modula Inc - Maine
old_description: Transform your material handling with the most advanced automated storage and retrieval systems from Modula.
about:
Modula Inc. operates from Lewiston, Maine, where it was founded in 1991. The privately held company designs and manufactures automated storage and retrieval systems, including vertical lift modules (VLMs), vertical carousels, and high-speed bin-picking solutions for industrial and commercial warehouses.

The product line centers on vertical lift modules such as the Modula Next, the high-throughput Modula Flexibox capable of processing up to 180 bins per hour, and the Modula Pallet for euro-pallet handling. Systems are built in the United States and sold through a network of more than 70 dealers across North America. The company reports more than 20,000 installations worldwide and 35-plus years of experience in warehouse automation.

Customers span aerospace, naval, biomedical, pharmaceutical, firearms, hospitality, automotive, e-commerce, electronics, food and beverage, and maritime sectors. Reference installations include Dassault Falcon Jet, GF Machining Solutions, Innomed, Rotor Clip, Symrise, Walser BMW, and Enercon Technologies.

Modula emphasizes U.S. manufacturing, local dealer support, and software integration with existing warehouse management and ERP systems. The company cites continual technology investment and ergonomic design as key differentiators.

name: Module Master
old_description: Module Master is a re-manufacturer of automotive and transportation related electronics. We rebuild electronics to a higher level of quality and reliability than OEM, for a fraction of the costs of an outright replacement. Located in Moscow Idaho USA our self-sufficient 7000 ft² facility is home to an extensive collection of testing equipment, engineering tools and manufacturing machines. Here our staff of talented professionals process the re-manufacturing and testing of your modules with a relentless focus on detail, quality control, and continued customer support. Our team is proud of its accomplishments, the services that we provide, the products that we produce, and delivering only the very best to our customers. We are totally dedicated to developing and maintaining this leading edge environment. To learn more about our work, please browse the products section of our website. We look forward to being a part of your current and future electronics re-manufacturing needs.
about:
Module Master was founded in 2004 by Gavin Curtis in Moscow, Idaho. The business began in a small pump house on his parents' property and has since grown into a remanufacturing operation with two facilities in Moscow, home to the University of Idaho.

The company specializes in rebuilding automotive electronic modules, including ABS controllers, instrument clusters, climate control units, power accessory modules, and powertrain control modules. Its technicians perform component-level repair, partial testing, and full remanufacturing using an array of testing equipment and manufacturing machines. The shop processes more than 1,000 modules each month across its two locations.

Module Master serves the automotive and transportation sectors, covering cars, trucks, motorcycles, ATVs, UTVs, and RVs. Its customers range from individual vehicle owners to independent repair shops such as K‑Tech Automotive and ABS Automotive in San Mateo, California.

The company states that its remanufactured modules meet or exceed OEM quality at a fraction of the cost of new replacements, positioning the service as a sustainable alternative. It emphasizes a focus on detail, quality control, and ongoing customer support.
